html:
The Yellowknives, or T'atsaot'ine, are a Dene people of the Northwest Territories of Canada, from the land north and east of Great Slave Lake. Their name comes from the copper tools they made from local deposits.

They speak a Dene (Athabaskan) language and lived by hunting caribou and fishing, moving through the boreal forest and the edge of the tundra. They traded copper and furs, first through Chipewyan middlemen and then with the Hudson's Bay Company and its rivals. They clashed with the Inuit to the north and with the Tłı̨chǫ to the west.

Their leader Akaitcho guided and fed the British explorer John Franklin on his first Arctic overland expedition, from 1819 to 1822. Epidemics in the 1800s cut their numbers, and many merged with Dënesųłinë́ neighbours. The city of Yellowknife, capital of the Northwest Territories, is named after them.
